videos.title: The Siege That Killed 13,000 British Soldiers — And Nobody Remembers
videos.description:
The Siege of Kut was not just a defeat — it was a catastrophe buried by history.

In this video, we follow the British advance into Mesopotamia, the failed push toward Baghdad, the siege of Kut al-Amara, and the surrender of more than 13,000 British and Indian troops to the Ottoman Empire in 1916. From starvation inside the town to the disastrous relief attempts outside it, this is the story of one of the most devastating Allied failures of World War I.

Why is Kut so forgotten? And how did a disaster of this scale vanish from public memory?

🎖️ Inside this episode:
• The British invasion of Mesopotamia  
• General Charles Townshend and the road to Kut  
• The Battle of Ctesiphon and the retreat  
• Starvation, disease, and collapse inside the siege  
• The failed relief operations that cost 23,000 casualties  
• The first military air supply mission in history  
• The surrender at Kut and the death march into captivity  
• Why Indian soldiers bore the greatest burden — and why they were forgotten

videos.title: The Siege That Destroyed Japan's Greatest Army — And Nobody Remembers
videos.description:
⚔️ The Battle of Imphal and Kohima was one of the most decisive clashes of World War II — and one of its most overlooked. In 1944, Japan launched a massive invasion of India through some of the harshest terrain on earth, convinced victory would come in weeks. Instead, the offensive collapsed into starvation, disease, mutiny, and annihilation.

From the siege of Imphal to the brutal fighting on Kohima’s tennis court, this is the story of the campaign that shattered Japan’s offensive power in Asia and left behind the infamous “Road of Bones.”

Why is a battle this enormous almost forgotten today?

🎖️ In this video:
• Japan’s disastrous Operation U-Go  
• Renya Mutaguchi’s fatal gamble  
• William Slim and the strategy that turned the war  
• The siege of Imphal  
• Kohima’s savage close-quarters combat  
• Starvation, collapse, and the Road of Bones  
• Why this turning point of WWII faded from public memory

videos.title: 300 British Riflemen vs 57 Tanks — The Night That Broke Rommel
videos.description:
🏜️ A shallow depression in the desert. 300 men. 19 anti-tank guns. No resupply. No relief. And wave after wave of Axis armor.

This episode tells the story of Outpost Snipe, one of the fiercest and most overlooked actions of El Alamein. In October 1942, Lieutenant Colonel Victor Turner and the 2nd Rifle Brigade dug in far ahead of the British line and found themselves surrounded by German and Italian tanks. What followed was an all-day battle of point-blank anti-tank fire, chaos, misidentification, friendly fire, burning vehicles, and extraordinary stubbornness under pressure.

At the center of it all is Turner himself, wounded but still moving from gun to gun, and at one critical moment helping load a six-pounder as enemy tanks closed in through the smoke. Outpost Snipe became a brutal test of whether infantry and anti-tank crews could stop massed armor in prepared positions—and the answer helped shape the battle of El Alamein.

videos.title: The Attack That Destroyed Japan's Entire Army in Burma
videos.description:
How did a missing zero help doom Japan’s army in Burma?

In this episode, Redoubt follows the Battle of Meiktila and the brilliant campaign of William Slim’s Fourteenth Army—an operation built on deception, speed, armor, and air power. While Japanese commanders focused on Mandalay, a massive Allied column slipped through the Gangaw Valley, crossed the Irrawaddy, and struck deep at Meiktila, the logistical heart of central Burma. What followed was one of the most decisive and underrated victories of the Second World War.

From the disaster of the 1942 retreat to the triumphs at Imphal, Kohima, Mandalay, and Meiktila, this is the story of how the “Forgotten Army” shattered the Japanese position in Burma and opened the road to Rangoon.

📌 In this video:
• The British collapse in Burma in 1942  
• How William Slim rebuilt the Fourteenth Army  
• Imphal and Kohima as the turning point  
• Operation Extended Capital and the deception plan  
• The drive on Meiktila and the failed Japanese response  
• Why the fall of Meiktila broke Japan’s army in Burma

videos.title: The British Trap That Fed Japan's Army to the Crocodiles
videos.description:
🐊 A thousand Japanese soldiers entered the mangrove swamps of Ramree Island in 1945. By the time it was over, the story had become one of the most infamous and disputed horrors of World War II.

In this episode, we dig into the Battle of Ramree Island, the British Fourteenth Army, William Slim’s forgotten Burma campaign, and the terrifying legend of soldiers trapped in crocodile-infested marshland. How much of the massacre story is true? How much was myth, memory, and wartime chaos? And what really happened in that swamp?

From naval bombardments and jungle warfare to conflicting survivor counts and the origins of the crocodile narrative, this is the full story behind one of history’s darkest battlefield legends.
